title: Describe features, advantages and benefits of a range of products

lessons.title: Features, advantages and benefits explained
lessons.html:
Features, advantages and benefits explained

Farmers do not buy seed because of a long list of technical facts. They buy it because they believe it will help them make more money, reduce risk or make farming easier. The FAB method helps a sales representative turn product facts into reasons to buy.

The three parts

TermMeaningSeed example
FeatureA fact about the productThis maize hybrid has a short growing season
AdvantageWhat the feature doesIt reaches maturity earlier than a full-season hybrid
BenefitWhat it means for this customerYou can plant later after the first good rains and still harvest before frost on your farm

A feature is true for every customer. A benefit depends on the customer's situation. The same early-maturing hybrid may be a strong benefit to a farmer in the eastern Free State with a short frost-free season, but less important to a farmer under irrigation in a warmer area.

Typical seed features

  • Yield potential in trials in different regions
  • Maturity class and drought tolerance
  • Disease resistance or tolerance, for example to grey leaf spot or rust
  • Herbicide or insect tolerance traits, where approved
  • Grain quality, such as milling quality for wheat or white maize for the food market
  • Standability and lodging resistance
  • Seed treatment included

Bridge phrases

Use phrases that link a feature to a benefit: 'which means that', 'so that you can', 'this helps you to'. For example: 'This cultivar has good rust resistance, which means you may need fewer fungicide applications, so that your cost per hectare is lower.'

Always use facts that you can support with trial data or official information. Never promise yields or results that are not proven. Under consumer protection law, misleading claims can lead to complaints and legal action.

lessons.title: Describing a range of products to customers
lessons.html:
Describing a range of products to customers

Most seed companies offer a range: several maize hybrids, soybean and wheat cultivars, pasture seed and vegetable seed. The skill is to match the right product to each customer and explain its benefits clearly.

Know your range

  • Study the product catalogue and technical sheets for every product you sell.
  • Know the trial results from your region and from independent trials such as those run by the Agricultural Research Council where available.
  • Know how products in the range compare with each other: which is best for dryland, which for irrigation, which for high-potential soils.
  • Know the competitors' products and be fair when comparing.
  • Know prices, pack sizes and availability.

Find the customer's needs first

Ask questions before you talk about products: What area do you plant? Dryland or irrigation? What was your yield last season? What problems did you have, such as drought, disease or frost? Who do you sell to? Listen carefully. Then choose two or three products that fit and describe them using FAB.

Example

A commercial farmer near Bothaville plants dryland maize on sandy soil and lost yield in a dry January. You might say: 'This hybrid has shown stable yields in dryland trials on sandy soils in your area (feature). It handles moisture stress during flowering better than many hybrids (advantage). That gives you more certainty of a crop in a dry season, which protects your cash flow (benefit).'

Handling questions

  • Answer honestly. If you do not know, say so and promise to find out.
  • Show trial data in simple tables or graphs.
  • Explain limitations too, for example a hybrid that is not suited to very late planting. Customers trust honest advisers and come back.

Key points

  • Feature = fact; advantage = what it does; benefit = what it means to this customer.
  • Benefits depend on the customer's needs, so ask and listen first.
  • Know the full range, trial results and competitor products.
  • Use bridge phrases to link features to benefits.
  • Only make claims you can support; never mislead.
